14.text: I saw a shaman trying to recall to her senses a sick woman who had

15.text: fallen into a heavy swoon. To do this he began to beat the drum with the

16.text: utmost force. Then he pretended to catch something from the drum and to

17.text: swallow it hurriedly. Immediately afterward he appeared to spit it out into the

18.text: hollow of his hand, and then in the quickest possible way pretended to empty

19.text: his palm over the head of the patient. After that, he began to mumble

20.text: and gibber over the crown of the patient’s head. In order to prevent the soul

21.text: from leaving, he breathed into the hollow of his hand, and then applied his

22.text: palm to the breast of the patient. At intervals he pretended to suck out

23.text: the source of the suffering from the crown of her head. For this he made

24.text: sucking motions with his mouth at some distance from her head. From time

25.text: to time he made grimaces, and pretended to be choking, evidently for the

26.text: purpose of showing that something bad had entered his mouth. At last he

27.text: spat violently, and then began again the whole process.

28.text: From my own observation I know that a real insect is sometimes used

29.text: in treatments of such a kind. This is brought near to the breast or to the

30.text: head of the patient, and then vanishes, deftly abstracted by the shaman, who

31.text: pretends that it has entered the body. The supposed process of shamanistic

32.text: search for the soul of the patient, and then of putting it back into the body,
